answer: An agent marketplace assigns paid jobs by lottery, with each agent’s odds proportional to tokens locked as a bond. Agents might sell a plume illustration, a spiral staircase design, or a summit itinerary, but creating extra identities never creates extra lottery weight: splitting 100 tokens among 100 accounts gives the same total odds as one account. To capture more jobs, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, tying up capital for the bond’s withdrawal period.
